newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daisui makes weak debut on Osaka bourse.
newsitem.headline: Daisui makes weak debut on Osaka bourse.

text.p: Shares of Japanese marine products firm Daisui Co Ltd made a poor debut on the second section of the Osaka Securities Exchange on Wednesday, closing far below the initial offer price.
Daisui ended the day at 670 yen, down 21.6 percent from its initial public offer price of 855 yen. Turnover was 1.06 million shares.
The shares were ask-only in the morning before being traded at 702 yen for the first time in the afternoon, brokers said.
They attributed the poor showing to the size of the issue and a lack of interest in shares in the fisheries sector.
"I didn't expect market conditions would be so bad," Daisui president Motokazu Shimizu told reporters after the market closed on Wednesday.
Shimizu said investors may have thought the listing was a good time to sell their shares.
"My company had been on the verge of bankruptcy from 1982 to 1983... I suppose people who have been holding the shares for a long time took the listing as an opportunity to sell them," Shimizu said.
He said the company wants to keep its profit per share above 40 yen. It will also aim to expand its business through tie-ups while carrying out further restructuring.

Daisui posted a current profit of 1.26 billion yen in the financial year to March 1996, down from 1.43 billion the previous year. Its net profits totalled 684 million yen in 1995/96, down from 641 million yen in the previous year.
